options.text: Heating makes the particles vibrate more until they leave fixed positions; that temperature is the melting point at atmospheric pressure.
Heating packs the particles closer until they stop vibrating; that temperature is the melting point.
Heating turns the solid butter straight into vapour; the melting point is the boiling temperature.
The butter melts at any temperature as soon as Harsh stirs it.

stem:
The diagram shows Harsh heating solid butter in a dish. A thermometer is placed in the butter. At one fixed temperature the solid butter turns into liquid butter.

Which claim is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Added heat increases particle vibration until particles leave fixed positions; that temperature at atmospheric pressure is the melting point.
teacher.figure_note: Dish of solid butter over gentle heat with a thermometer.
